newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm on vote and auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm on vote and auction hopes.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer across the board on Monday due to a calm outcome to local elections and expectations that primary rates would be unchanged, traders said.
"The market was liquid today. Local elections going ahead peacefully helped, as did forecasts that primary rates will be relatively unchanged tomorrow," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and the 24-hour contract closed 1.3 and one centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8950/7.8990 and 7.8900/7.8950 per dollar.
"Dealers who had gone long (in dollars) over the weekend ahead of the elections stepped in to sell dollars today, but volume was really thin," the trader added.

Elections were held on Sunday to renew local congresses and city halls in the states of Mexico, Coahuila and Hidalgo. The state of Mexico, which borders Mexico City, was considered particularly important as it the most populous in the country and is heavily industrialized.
There was no same-day trading on Monday as U.S. banks were closed for Veterans' Day. Dealers noted that trade was light for the same reason.

Traders expected results to be mixed at Tuesday's primary Cetes auction. The bellwether 28-day Cete was expected to either be unchanged or gain slightly, while longer term issues were seen down slightly.
"Any movement in (primary Cetes) rates has already been discounted, and we do not expect U.S. rates to change at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Wednesday," said a trader.
Dealers expected the peso to be stable on Tuesday, with 48-hour contracts trading between 7.88 and 7.91 per dollar.
"Some foreigners may step in to buy dollars tomorrow because they are cheap (in peso terms). We don't expect rates to vary much, but we do see volume increasing," said a dealer.
